title: sixteen ways of spelling a valueOf that reads a capability all charge the same row to the function that coerces the object, so the top-level call is refused for that capability sixteen times
notes: specification/requirements.mdx, 'Inference': 'Calling a function with unsatisfied requirements MUST add those capabilities to the caller's R row' and 'Requirement inference MUST be transitive through ordinary calls.' A coercion is a call the language makes on the author's behalf: `+obj` invokes `obj.valueOf()`, that member has a row, and the row must reach the function that wrote the `+`. Nothing in that obligation mentions how the member was SPELLED, and this case is the statement that nothing may. WHY THIS CASE EXISTS: on 2026-08-27 a lane closed 116 coercion divergences between the two backends while conformance reported 0 divergent throughout, because the corpus had no case in which a coercion member was spelled any way other than a method shorthand or a class method. Ten of the sixteen spellings here were fail-open on at least one backend before that work — the row was simply lost, the program compiled, and reading the capability panicked at run time. That is the gap this case closes, and it closes it as an EQUALITY rather than as a list: the last six spellings are the ones both backends already charged, so the promise is 'these ten answer the same as those six', which is a statement a future refactor cannot satisfy by making the whole family silent. The ten are chosen to hit distinct resolution mechanisms so that a fix which under- or over-fires anywhere turns this case red: an arrow and a function-expression property value (a member whose declaration is an initializer rather than a method); a computed key written as a string literal and one written through a `const` binding (the name has to be constant-folded); a property holding a REFERENCE to a function declared elsewhere (resolution has to follow the binding, not read the object literal); a shorthand property (the name and the value are one token); a class ARROW FIELD, which is an instance property and not on the prototype; the object reached through a nested property and through a `const` alias (two binding hops before the object is even in hand); and a GETTER named `valueOf` whose inferred return type is a function, which is the shape where the member is produced by running another member. WHAT THIS CASE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT PIN: three further spellings measured on both backends and NOT declared here — an explicitly annotated `declared-type-annotation`, an annotated getter return, and a helper that returns the object. All three are accepted by BOTH backends today, which is a shared fail-open recorded as residual R1, and declaring them would either freeze a bug or need an `xfail` on both sides. It also does not pin the ORDER of the sixteen diagnostics: the judge compares a sorted multiset, and the two backends do not promise an emission order. `messageContains` is declared on the FIRST diagnostic only, and its job is to hold the whole set to the right capability: sixteen refusals at sixteen positions are satisfied by code and position alone even if the row named something else entirely, and one capability name is enough to pin that because every one of the sixteen charges the same Db. It is the bare name because the two backends render a row differently (`Db` versus `{Db}`). VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: mutating the FIRST declared line from 79 to 78 — one line up, onto the `export const charged = [` line, which is what a backend that anchored a top-level call at its statement would report — turns the case red on BOTH backends with the position diff printed, and the file was restored byte-identically (sha256 0af2347a6edb52d74c6256b19b4fd6b75408a4d89bece44a15a3113f4c6c8b4b before and after, that digest being this file's content at the moment the mutation ran — the sentence recording it is appended afterwards, so the shipped file necessarily hashes differently). The paired positive controls are `the-coercion-row-reaches-the-provide-site-and-runs`, where six of these spellings are provided a layer and must RUN, and `coercion-members-that-never-run-charge-nothing`, which holds seven positions where a Db-reading member is in reach and must still charge nothing.
